effectiveTerms: MAME licence (non-commercial) over ISC, with MIT and Apache-2.0 components
note: ares is ISC. The Nintendo 64's display processor is ares' own paraLLEl-RDP (MIT), loaded through volk (MIT) against the Vulkan headers (Apache-2.0), all vendored inside ares, or, when a project chooses the Software renderer, angrylion's rasteriser, which descends from MESS and carries the MAME licence: redistribution is permitted, sale and commercial use are not. Both are in the one built core, so it is distributable under those terms and no others - the same shape as the gpgx, opera and snes9x packages. The core drew with angrylion until 2026-11-02 too (from TASEmulators' copy then); since 2026-11-03 it is angrylion's own upstream, beside paraLLEl-RDP rather than instead of it (chimera#481).

components.name: paraLLEl-RDP
components.note: The Nintendo 64's display processor, on the frontend's Vulkan device through miniBox's bridge; vendored inside ares (ares/n64/vulkan/parallel-rdp), with Granite's Vulkan backend.

components.name: angrylion RDP Plus
components.note: The Nintendo 64's display processor rasterised in software, for a project whose renderer is Software (chimera#481). Its core only (src/core), with one patch (patches/angrylion-rdp-plus); the source of every component of the built core is public at the URLs in this file.

components.name: volk
components.note: paraLLEl-RDP's Vulkan loader; its licence is at the end of the header.

components.name: sljit
components.note: ares' recompiler back end, used by the Nintendo 64's CPU and RSP unless a project asks for the interpreters.

components.name: TZXFile
components.note: Reached through mia, ares' media loader.

components.name: ymfm
components.note: Yamaha FM sound chips, reached through the Famicom's expansion audio and the Neo Geo's.

components.name: qon / qoi2
components.note: The video codec ares uses for LaserActive media; compiled in because the PC Engine and Mega Drive cores reference it.
